title: Teen completes seven GCSE exams over five months with his eyes

evidence_packet.title: Teen completes seven GCSE exams over five months with his eyes
evidence_packet.lead: Patrick spent five months filling out his GCSE exam papers using eye-tracking technology
evidence_packet.summary: Patrick spent five months filling out his GCSE exam papers using eye-tracking technology
evidence_packet.evidence_text: For many teenagers awaiting their GCSE results on Thursday, sitting their exam papers took place over several weeks - but for one 16-year-old from Cheshire, the whole process took months while they used their eye-gaze to answer the questions Patrick, 16, has cerebral palsy and completed his exams over the course of five months using eye-tracking technology As a student at The Fallibroome Academy, in Macclesfield, Patrick began filling out exam papers for his seven GCSEs in February and completed them in June Ahead of results day Patrick told BBC Breakfast : "My ultimate dream is to work in media and to be the next Claire Balding on wheels." Patrick said he was inspired after seeing the late Rob Burrow, a rugby league player who had motor neurone disease (MND), appear on an episode of CBeebies Bedtime Stories, narrating the story using a computer to speak Patrick, who also uses a computer to speak, was able to complete his exams by using eye-gaze tracking technology

title: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife

evidence_packet.title: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife
evidence_packet.lead: Victim Support helped Trish through court proceedings after sexual abuse she suffered as a child
evidence_packet.summary: Victim Support helped Trish through court proceedings after sexual abuse she suffered as a child
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife - BBC News Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig says seeing Trish go through the court process made him want to give something back to Victim Support By Haider Saleem North West Published 1 hour ago A father who had never boxed has raised £2,630 for a charity supporting people affected by crime - after it helped his wife through court proceedings over sexual abuse she suffered as a child. Craig Hinde, 41, from Droylsden, Greater Manchester, trained for eight weeks before taking part in a white-collar boxing event in Manchester. His wife Trish said Victim Support prepared her for court after she reported being sexually abused as a child by her father, Gerard King, who was convicted at Chester Crown Court in 2022. Craig also said it had helped their son Jacob, 10, who took up boxing after being bullied, regain his sparring confidence, showing how trying mattered more than winning. Trish, 38, said she had never been in a courtroom before and described the prospect as "terrifying". The lettings administrator said Victim Support talked her through what to expect and reassured her that it was acceptable to say she did not know or could not remember an answer. "For people who have been through trauma, they often are terrified of not being believed," she said. But she said there was none of that feeling when speaking to the charity. "It's just acceptance and validation," she said. "There's no judgment. They just help you through the process." Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig said he had avoided physical exercise since injuring his knees at 17 Trish said getting help was "the best thing I ever did" and that she was now a very different person from the one who had gone through the court process

evidence_packet.title: 'Gentle giant' died after medication withdrawn, inquest told
evidence_packet.lead: James Snowden, a keen sportsman, had struggled with suicidal feelings since his childhood
evidence_packet.summary: James Snowden, a keen sportsman, had struggled with suicidal feelings since his childhood
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A keen rugby player and strongman described by his mother as a "gentle giant" had a prescription for anti-psychotic medication withdrawn weeks before his death, an inquest heard James Snowden, who had struggled with suicidal feelings since childhood, was 21 when his body was found at his family home in Altrincham in December 2024 Manchester South Coroner's Court heard after numerous attempts to take his own life he had been prescribed sulpiride in 2021 - which his mother said had helped him "pursue a full life" When James died he was under the care of the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which will give evidence throughout the week and has been approached for comment However, the court heard that on 26 November 2024, James had attended an appointment to plan for the gradual withdrawal of the drug Snowden, a keen sportsman, had been a member of Broughton Park FC and Sale FC Rugby Clubs and St Lawrence's Gaelic Football Club

title: Murder inquiry after man dies two days after Manchester stabbing

evidence_packet.title: Murder inquiry after man dies two days after Manchester stabbing
evidence_packet.lead: A 29-year-old woman is being questioned on suspicion of murder and assaulting a police officer
evidence_packet.summary: A 29-year-old woman is being questioned on suspicion of murder and assaulting a police officer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Murder inquiry after man dies two days after Manchester stabbing - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, A 29-year-old woman, initially arrested on suspicion of wounding, has been further detained on suspicion of murder By Jonny Humphries North West Published 17 August 2026 A murder investigation has been launched after a man died two days after he was stabbed in the leg. The 36-year-old was found injured at a house on Berwyn Avenue in Blackley, Manchester, at 02:45 BST on Saturday following reports of a disturbance. He was taken to hospital but died from his injuries on Monday morning. A 29-year-old woman, who was initially arrested on suspicion of wounding and assaulting a police officer, was now being questioned on suspicion of murder, Greater Manchester Police said. The force previously said the police officer was not seriously hurt. Det Insp Terina Arthern said the suspect and victim were known to each other and described the attack as an "isolated incident" with "no threat to the wider community". "I would like to express my sincere condolences to the victim in this case," she said. "We have informed his next-of-kin and our thoughts remain with his family and friends. "Our investigation has been moving at pace since the weekend to establish the facts." The fish were found in the River Tame following the blaze off Wellington Road in Greenfield, on Sunday, The Environment Agency said. The foam was described by the agency as "firewater run off", which is left-over from the foam firefighters used to tackle the fire. A spokesperson said: "Although containment measures were taken, some firewater run-off entered the river. Officers recorded several hundred dead fish in the affected area, however this morning they found no additional fish fatalities." The spokesperson continued: "Surface foam remains visible. However, it appears to be dispersing downstream. "We will continue to monitor the situation and assess any ongoing environmental impacts." Image source, Craig Hannah Image caption, Swathes of foam were spotted in the River Tame Craig Hannah, 57, lives close by and witnessed the blaze- which began just after 07:30 BST on Sunday. "It was quite frightening. I live around 70 metres away from it. Luckily we were downwind," he said. "It was just the road closures, the proximity to other people's houses that was quite worrying." Residents have since returned to their homes, but Craig said there was alarm at the state of the river. title: Piccadilly Gardens revamp to start 'soon as possible'

evidence_packet.title: Piccadilly Gardens revamp to start 'soon as possible'
evidence_packet.lead: The council says work will begin as soon as possible if the scheme is approved this autumn
evidence_packet.summary: The council says work will begin as soon as possible if the scheme is approved this autumn
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Long-awaited plans to transform a major public space in the centre of a city have been submitted Ten months on from the proposals first being revealed, Manchester City Council has put in a planning bid to create more lawns, plant more trees and create a larger playground for families in Piccadilly Gardens The authority said work could begin "as soon as possible" if planning permission was granted in the autumn Hundreds of people responded to a consultation on the plans, with some raising concerns about continued anti-social behaviour at the site, and questioning how it would be kept safe for those who would want to use it Under the plans, old fountains, low concrete walls and raised planters will be removed, while lighting, sightlines and CCTV will be improved Of those who took part in the consultation, 58% believed the proposals would create a safe and welcoming space, 67% said they would provide clear walking routes, and 70% thought they would make it greener and more colourful

title: Man charged after Salford rooftop stand-off ends

evidence_packet.title: Man charged after Salford rooftop stand-off ends
evidence_packet.lead: Simon Harris, 37, has been charged after a man was arrested on a Salford rooftop on Saturday
evidence_packet.summary: Simon Harris, 37, has been charged after a man was arrested on a Salford rooftop on Saturday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has been charged after police ended a two-day stand-off by climbing a ladder to arrest a sleeping suspect on a roof Greater Manchester Police released footage showing the moment an officer climbed the ladder onto the roof of a back porch in Ash Street, Salford, and grabbed a man, who was lying down The man was pulled down the ladder, with his trousers appearing to fall down, before being arrested by officers in the garden of the property on Saturday Simon Harris, 37, has been charged with four counts of criminal damage, two counts of assault of an emergency worker, intentionally/recklessly causing a public nuisance, burglary dwelling and theft He is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court later Detective Chief Inspector Helen Bagnall thanked members of the public following the man's arrest, which came after a two-day emergency service response

title: Altrincham mum warns of 'botched' £150 filler that cost £700 to fix

evidence_packet.title: Altrincham mum warns of 'botched' £150 filler that cost £700 to fix
evidence_packet.lead: Joanne Bauer says she stayed home for weeks after the cheap treatment affected her confidence
evidence_packet.summary: Joanne Bauer says she stayed home for weeks after the cheap treatment affected her confidence
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother-of-two said she refused to go out for weeks after "botched" under-eye fillers left her in searing pain - and has now urged others considering similar treatments to do careful research Joanne Bauer, 48, said she chose a £150 treatment she spotted on social media after being quoted about £495 elsewhere, and later had to spend more than £700 having it corrected "I wished I'd done some more homework" the finance director from Altrincham, Greater Manchester, said Her warning comes as a poll commissioned by the Professional Standards Authority for Health and Social Care found 46% of 1,000 UK adults surveyed believed all aesthetic practitioners were regulated by law The non-surgical aesthetics industry - including providers of Botox, dermal fillers, and chemical peels - is largely unregulated. In the UK, anyone can legally perform many non-surgical procedures without medical qualifications Last year the government promised to develop a licensing system for England, but it is yet to be introduced

title: Former Bolton footballer and family speak out about daughter's death

evidence_packet.title: Former Bolton footballer and family speak out about daughter's death
evidence_packet.lead: Dean Holden and his wife Danielle have spoken about their loss as they launch a new YouTube series
evidence_packet.summary: Dean Holden and his wife Danielle have spoken about their loss as they launch a new YouTube series
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former Premier League footballer whose daughter died from meningococcal septicaemia have said they hope that by speaking out about their loss they can help others in the same situation Dean Holden and Danielle Nicholls lost their daughter Cici, aged 17 months, after she contracted meningococcal septicaemia , external while they were on holiday in Lanzarote in May 2012 Nicholls said it was important for the couple to talk openly about their "devastating" loss as they launch their new YouTube reality series charting their family life "warts and all" The mum-of-five told BBC Breakfast that her other four children "have saved my life" and "are my happiness and... my sunshine" She said the family used humour as a way to help them to cope with their loss and "I think that that's how you have to move forward", adding that "you have to see the brighter side (of life)" She said: "I didn't want the kids to think life was great and then our sister died, and life was horrible and it's so difficult because there is such sadness."

evidence_packet.summary: An industrial unit near Oldham erupted in flames, with 45 homes evacuated
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Families had to be evacuated from their homes in two streets after a huge fire broke out at a neighbouring industrial building The blaze, which shot huge plumes of black and orange smoke into the sky, was spotted at just after 07:30 BST at a site off Wellington Road in Greenfield, near Oldham Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said 45 homes were evacuated in Wellington Road and Knoll Close, which backs on to the burning building Residents have now returned to their homes, with fire crews using gas detectors to ensure it was safe to do so, a spokesperson said More than 10 fire engines along with a number of aerial ladder units and specialist appliances from across Greater Manchester were sent to the scene of the blaze "Our crews remain at the scene, continuing their work alongside partners to make the site safe," the fire service added

evidence_packet.evidence_text: For many teenagers awaiting their GCSE results on Thursday, sitting their exam papers took place over several weeks - but for one 16-year-old from Cheshire, the whole process took months while they used their eye-gaze to answer the questions Patrick, 16, has cerebral palsy and completed his exams over the course of five months using eye-tracking technology As a student at The Fallibroome Academy, in Macclesfield, Patrick began filling out exam papers for his seven GCSEs in February and completed them in June Ahead of results day Patrick told BBC Breakfast : "My ultimate dream is to work in media and to be the next Claire Balding on wheels." Patrick said he was inspired after seeing the late Rob Burrow, a rugby league player who had motor neurone disease (MND), appear on an episode of CBeebies Bedtime Stories, narrating the story using a computer to speak Patrick, who also uses a computer to speak, was able to complete his exams by using eye-gaze tracking technology

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A father who had never boxed has raised £2,630 for a charity supporting people affected by crime - after it helped his wife through court proceedings over sexual abuse she suffered as a child Craig Hinde, 41, from Droylsden, Greater Manchester, trained for eight weeks before taking part in a white-collar boxing event in Manchester His wife Trish said Victim Support prepared her for court after she reported being sexually abused as a child by her father, Gerard King, who was convicted at Chester Crown Court in 2022 Craig also said it had helped their son Jacob, 10, who took up boxing after being bullied, regain his sparring confidence, showing how trying mattered more than winning Trish, 38, said she had never been in a courtroom before and described the prospect as "terrifying" The lettings administrator said Victim Support talked her through what to expect and reassured her that it was acceptable to say she did not know or could not remember an answer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A keen rugby player and strongman described by his mother as a "gentle giant" had a prescription for anti-psychotic medication withdrawn weeks before his death, an inquest heard James Snowden, who had struggled with suicidal feelings since childhood, was 21 when his body was found at his family home in Altrincham in December 2024 Manchester South Coroner's Court heard after numerous attempts to take his own life he had been prescribed sulpiride in 2021 - which his mother said had helped him "pursue a full life" When James died he was under the care of the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which will give evidence throughout the week and has been approached for comment However, the court heard that on 26 November 2024, James had attended an appointment to plan for the gradual withdrawal of the drug Snowden, a keen sportsman, had been a member of Broughton Park FC and Sale FC Rugby Clubs and St Lawrence's Gaelic Football Club

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hundreds of fish have been found dead after a fire at an industrial unit caused masses of foam to run into a nearby river The fish were found in the River Tame following the blaze off Wellington Road in Greenfield, on Sunday, The Environment Agency said The foam was described by the agency as "firewater run off", which is left-over from the foam firefighters used to tackle the fire A spokesperson said: "Although containment measures were taken, some firewater run-off entered the river. title: Piccadilly Gardens revamp to start 'soon as possible'

evidence_packet.title: Piccadilly Gardens revamp to start 'soon as possible'
evidence_packet.lead: Long-awaited plans to transform a major public space in the centre of a city have been submitted Ten months on from the proposals first being revealed, Manchester City Council has put in a planning bid to create more lawns, plant more trees and create a larger playground for fami
evidence_packet.summary: Long-awaited plans to transform a major public space in the centre of a city have been submitted Ten months on from the proposals first being revealed, Manchester City Council has put in a planning bid to create more lawns, plant more trees and create a larger playground for fami
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Long-awaited plans to transform a major public space in the centre of a city have been submitted Ten months on from the proposals first being revealed, Manchester City Council has put in a planning bid to create more lawns, plant more trees and create a larger playground for families in Piccadilly Gardens The authority said work could begin "as soon as possible" if planning permission was granted in the autumn Hundreds of people responded to a consultation on the plans, with some raising concerns about continued anti-social behaviour at the site, and questioning how it would be kept safe for those who would want to use it Under the plans, old fountains, low concrete walls and raised planters will be removed, while lighting, sightlines and CCTV will be improved Of those who took part in the consultation, 58% believed the proposals would create a safe and welcoming space, 67% said they would provide clear walking routes, and 70% thought they would make it greener and more colourful

As an updated local list aims to safeguard everything from Victorian pubs to vintage post boxes, historic preservation is back on the agenda for the centena Comments News Neal Keeling C
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past? As an updated local list aims to safeguard everything from Victorian pubs to vintage post boxes, historic preservation is back on the agenda for the centena Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:59, 18 Aug 2026 It has come too late for The Ambassador. Sat at the top of Langworthy Road it had a 2,000 capacity, and a marble staircase in the foyer. The exterior was clad in faience tiles and decorated with Art Deco and Italianate Opened on Christmas Eve 1928 it was one of the first "super cinemas" outside London. It had a huge stage for live variety shows and an orchestra pit It was where Violet Carson's showbiz career began. She played the piano there before becoming a national institution as Ena Sharples in Coronation Street View 15 Images The Ambassador cinema built in 1928 in Langworthy Road, Salford, which became a bingo hall in the mid 60s. Despite a campaign by locals to save it the landmark was bulldozed in 2004 after the council stripped it of its Grade II listed status In 1965 it became a bingo hall but closed in 1995 after a new rival opened in Hankinson Way, Pendleton

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Nearly 200 new homes planned for 'beautiful' Oldham valley alongside new Metrolink stop The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Nearly 200 new homes could be built in a ‘beautiful’ valley as part of a major new development that includes a new Metrolink stop Plans have been submitted to Oldham Council asking for approval for up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley in Oldham. The scheme is being put forward by IDPartnership Northern on behalf of Barratt Homes Manchester The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. This is a long term plan across every borough in the region except Stockport to oversee housebuilding, create jobs, and protect green belt land from unplanned development In the wider plans for the area, around 2,000 new homes could be built alongside new industrial and warehouse space, a local centre, and new access to education facilities. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road as well as new Metrolink stop at Broadb The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans

evidence_packet.summary: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Mancheste
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Manchester Police officers mimicked and mocked the accent of a black female colleague at work then laughed about it, a misconduct hearing was told. It was said to have left the PC feeling 'upset and uncomfortable' The allegations, claim the force, involved 'unwanted, offensive, racist and disrespectful' language and behaviour One, a sergeant, is said to have compared a photograph of a female fraud suspect with curly hair and thick glasses to the PC's mother. The hearing was also told a PC described the officer's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' before smiling at her and walking away Named only as Pc Y, the alleged victim was born in Africa, but speaks fluent English. She joined GMP as a response officer based at Bury police station in May, 2019 The allegations against seven serving officers and two now former officers were made on November 1, 2023. All were based at Bury at the time

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford family left devastated after £6k luxury holiday to Egypt ruined by scammer "Your heads all over, you're flying out the day after, you've got kids to worry about." Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:51, 17 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Mar A family say they were left stranded on their luxury holiday after their hotel booking was cancelled by a scammer Tania Rowan booked a stay for six people at the Charmillion Club Resort in Egypt through package holiday provider, On the Beach The family from Salford was due to check in on August 5 and return on August 12. According to Tania, the day before she flew out, she was tricked out of £768 after calling a number and speaking to a man who she thought worked for On the Beach Tania, 51, had made the call after she was unable to log onto the On the Beach app to check the status of her booking ahead of the flight. She told the MEN how she found the number on Google with the help of her daughter While on a phone call with a person she presumed to be an On the Beach rep, she was told her account was short of £768

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Where 60,000 new homes could be built in Manchester The city's future is being decided. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:23, 17 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Strangeways is an area where new homes are planned (Image: Sean Han Manchester’s future until 2039 is about to be decided with a massive development plan getting closer to approval The council’s local plan has mapped out where up to 60,000 new homes will be built around the city, as well as how it will help create new jobs and places for business Places included in a ‘core growth area’ will take the bulk of work and have been earmarked for huge regeneration in future years, accounting for more than 42,000 new homes and 1.4 million sqm of office space This includes central Manchester where there are plans to expand the boundary of the city centre, as well as the areas of Holt Town near Ancoats and New Islington, Central Park near Harpurhey and Newton Heath, Sportcity in east Manchester, and part of the Victoria North project t The core growth area is the ‘economic hub’ of Greater Manchester and is ‘located at the heart of the transport connections across the north of England.’

As he fell, Andy managed to pull the duvet off his bed, waking his wife Bernadette, who called an ambulance. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Jailed, the drug kingpin nicknamed 'Knuckles' who ran 'Sonic' line targeting university students and Parklife Former railway engineer Akeel Knight-Pascoe, 33, ran at least four drugs lines Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:40, 17 Aug 202 Akeel Knight-Pascoe, 33, from Whalley Range , known as 'Knuckles', was behind four drugs lines named after characters from the popular video game, Sonic, Knuckles, Tails and Shadow. He promoted the lines on Snapchat and also with business cards and lighters which contained contac His team of dealers and accomplices mainly targeted university students living in Fallowfield , south Manchester, but they also supplied a vast array of drugs such as cocaine, ecstasy, 2CB and 'magic mushrooms' at large events such as Parklife, Manchester Crown Court was told Police in plain clothes first arrested him in Fallowfield in February 2022 when they spotted him on a mountain bike and detected the smell of cannabis. He dismounted and ran off but officers caught him following a brief foot chase on Landcross Road, prosecutor Gemma Maxwell told On him police found drugs including ecstasy and cocaine worth up to £700, lighters marketing the 'Sonic' drugs line and a plastic bag containing six mobile phones which, after they were analysed, revealed numerous messages related to drugs supply. He denied running the drugs line He was still on bail when he was arrested again in May 2025 after staff at a Travelodge hotel on Ducie Street in Manchester city centre became concerned about the smell of cannabis coming from his room. evidence_packet.title: Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court after a two-day stand-off with police who grabbed the sleeping suspect from a roof Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court. Harris, of no fixed address, who was not legally represented during the five-minute hearing, is accused of six offences between August 14 and 16 The offences include burglary – entering a property in Reservoir Street, Salford , Greater Manchester and stealing T-shirts and rum punch – according to charges read out in court He is also accused of two counts of assaulting an emergency worker – two police officers – intentionally causing a public nuisance by sitting on a roof, and two counts of criminal damage to separate properties Harris entered no pleas to the charges and bail was opposed by prosecutor Hannah Nicholls, who told the court the case was too serious to be dealt with at the magistrates' court

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Gorton Gorton knife attack sees boy, 15, stabbed in the back after getting off a bus Police want to speak to two people, one wearing a Manchester United coat, following the incident on June 1. News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:14, 17 Aug 2026 Vie Police investigating an alleged attack where a boy of 15 was stabbed in his back after stepping off a bus are appealing to the public to help trace two people The appeal follows a serious assault on the youngster moments after he stepped off a bus in Gorton at around 11.20pm on Monday June 1. The teen was allegedly attacked by two males The youngster suffered serious injuries 'consistent' with a knife attack, according to Greater Manchester Police . "Thankfully, his injuries were not life-threatening and he has since made a full recovery," the force said in a statement today as officers made their public appeal "One of the suspects is described as a black male, wearing a grey and green Manchester United coat with black trousers," said GMP Officers from GMP's Xcalibre Task Force, set up to tackle gang crime, are now appealing for information following the alleged 'Section 18' assault, also known as grievous bodily harm

title: From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past?

evidence_packet.title: From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past?
evidence_packet.lead: Salford From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past?
evidence_packet.summary: Salford From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past? As an updated local list aims to safeguard everything from Victorian pubs to vintage post boxes, historic preservation is back on the agenda for the centena Comments News Neal Keeling C
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford From lost super-cinemas to gasworks walls: Can Salford finally learn to love its past? As an updated local list aims to safeguard everything from Victorian pubs to vintage post boxes, historic preservation is back on the agenda for the centena Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:59, 18 Aug 2026 It has come too late for The Ambassador. Sat at the top of Langworthy Road it had a 2,000 capacity, and a marble staircase in the foyer. The exterior was clad in faience tiles and decorated with Art Deco and Italianate Opened on Christmas Eve 1928 it was one of the first "super cinemas" outside London. It had a huge stage for live variety shows and an orchestra pit It was where Violet Carson's showbiz career began. She played the piano there before becoming a national institution as Ena Sharples in Coronation Street View 15 Images The Ambassador cinema built in 1928 in Langworthy Road, Salford, which became a bingo hall in the mid 60s. Despite a campaign by locals to save it the landmark was bulldozed in 2004 after the council stripped it of its Grade II listed status In 1965 it became a bingo hall but closed in 1995 after a new rival opened in Hankinson Way, Pendleton

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Nearly 200 new homes planned for 'beautiful' Oldham valley alongside new Metrolink stop The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Nearly 200 new homes could be built in a ‘beautiful’ valley as part of a major new development that includes a new Metrolink stop Plans have been submitted to Oldham Council asking for approval for up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley in Oldham. The scheme is being put forward by IDPartnership Northern on behalf of Barratt Homes Manchester The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. This is a long term plan across every borough in the region except Stockport to oversee housebuilding, create jobs, and protect green belt land from unplanned development In the wider plans for the area, around 2,000 new homes could be built alongside new industrial and warehouse space, a local centre, and new access to education facilities. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road as well as new Metrolink stop at Broadb The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans

evidence_packet.summary: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Mancheste
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Manchester Police officers mimicked and mocked the accent of a black female colleague at work then laughed about it, a misconduct hearing was told. It was said to have left the PC feeling 'upset and uncomfortable' The allegations, claim the force, involved 'unwanted, offensive, racist and disrespectful' language and behaviour One, a sergeant, is said to have compared a photograph of a female fraud suspect with curly hair and thick glasses to the PC's mother. The hearing was also told a PC described the officer's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' before smiling at her and walking away Named only as Pc Y, the alleged victim was born in Africa, but speaks fluent English. She joined GMP as a response officer based at Bury police station in May, 2019 The allegations against seven serving officers and two now former officers were made on November 1, 2023. All were based at Bury at the time

He promoted the lines on Snapchat and also with business cards and lighters which contained contac His team of dealers and accomplices mainly targeted university students living in Fallowfield , south Manchester, but they also supplied a vast array of drugs such as cocaine, ecstasy, 2CB and 'magic mushrooms' at large events such as Parklife, Manchester Crown Court was told Police in plain clothes first arrested him in Fallowfield in February 2022 when they spotted him on a mountain bike and detected the smell of cannabis. He dismounted and ran off but officers caught him following a brief foot chase on Landcross Road, prosecutor Gemma Maxwell told On him police found drugs including ecstasy and cocaine worth up to £700, lighters marketing the 'Sonic' drugs line and a plastic bag containing six mobile phones which, after they were analysed, revealed numerous messages related to drugs supply. He denied running the drugs line He was still on bail when he was arrested again in May 2025 after staff at a Travelodge hotel on Ducie Street in Manchester city centre became concerned about the smell of cannabis coming from his room. evidence_packet.lead: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court after a two-day stand-off with police who grabbed the sleeping suspect from a roof Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court. Harris, of no fixed address, who was not legally represented during the five-minute hearing, is accused of six offences between August 14 and 16 The offences include burglary – entering a property in Reservoir Street, Salford , Greater Manchester and stealing T-shirts and rum punch – according to charges read out in court He is also accused of two counts of assaulting an emergency worker – two police officers – intentionally causing a public nuisance by sitting on a roof, and two counts of criminal damage to separate properties Harris entered no pleas to the charges and bail was opposed by prosecutor Hannah Nicholls, who told the court the case was too serious to be dealt with at the magistrates' court

title: Altrincham firm Cotton Traders grows revenue to £113.5m

evidence_packet.title: Altrincham firm Cotton Traders grows revenue to £113.5m
evidence_packet.lead: It remains one of Altrincham’s largest private-sector employers
evidence_packet.summary: It remains one of Altrincham’s largest private-sector employers
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It remains one of Altrincham’s largest private-sector employers Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Actor Will Mellor modelling Cotton Traders wear Altrincham-based clothing retailer Cotton Traders has reported higher revenue and operating profit, despite ongoing inflationary pressures Turnover rose 5.2% to £113.5m for the year to 27 December 2025, up from £107.9m in the previous period. Operating profit increased 8.5% to £10.3m, with EBITDA up 1% to £12.1m The company, which has its headquarters on Atlantic Street in Broadheath, attributed the growth to all channels It opened six new stores during the year, taking the estate to 94 sites, and added two new online marketplaces - George at Asda and Next - taking the total to five. Marketplace revenue rose 58% year on year. Online and catalogue sales together accounted for 76.3% of overall sales CEO Nick Hamblin said: “It’s promising to see a healthy increase in revenue for Cotton Traders this financial year in the face of continued inflation alongside wider macroeconomic trading conditions

title: 300 more school places for Altrincham secured as council buys Loreto Prep site

evidence_packet.lead: The first additional places are expected from September 2027
evidence_packet.summary: The first additional places are expected from September 2027
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The first additional places are expected from September 2027 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has completed the purchase of the former Loreto Preparatory School site on Dunham Road - ending years of uncertainty over the three-acre plot and securing it for the expansion of neighbouring North Cestrian School The acquisition, funded by a Department for Education capital grant, will allow North Cestrian to add up to 300 secondary school places A feasibility study is now underway, with the first additional places expected from September 2027 and the full expansion complete by September 2028 The deal was struck by Trafford's Development and Education teams working alongside Hamblin Education Trust, which runs North Cestrian It draws a line under a two-year campaign that began when Loreto Prep - an independent Catholic primary school with a 114-year history - unexpectedly closed in July 2023 , citing declining pupil numbers and financial pressures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: James Snowden, who had struggled with suicidal feelings since childhood, was 21 when his body was found at his family home in Altrincham in December 2024 Manchester South Coroner's Court heard after numerous attempts to take his own life he had been prescribed sulpiride in 2021 - which his mother said had helped him "pursue a full life" When James died he was under the care of the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which will give evidence throughout the week and has been approached for comment However, the court heard that on 26 November 2024, James had attended an appointment to plan for the gradual withdrawal of the drug Snowden, a keen sportsman, had been a member of Broughton Park FC and Sale FC Rugby Clubs and St Lawrence's Gaelic Football Club As a competitive strongman, in 2019 he reportedly became the second youngest person on record to lift the famed Dinnie Stones at the first attempt, unassisted, at The Gathering stone-lifting contest in Aberdeenshire, Scotland

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council's Community Safety Service was granted a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) following repeated offences targeting retailers in Chadderton

There are things that can be done in the interim period and that is what we would like to explore.” He added that increased travel times into locations in Manchester city centre and surrounding areas leave residents socially excluded, causing “barriers to employment, education, and social mobility”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

There’s five dates from now until the end of Pride weekend, and what better way to mark it than to reflect on what happened on the very cobbles we walk on that made way for such a joyful celebration. После аншлагов в Европе и США спектакль впервые приезжает в Лондон. 📍 University College London, Level 1, 20 Bedford Way, London WC1H 0AL 🕕 DOORS: 18:00 🕖 SHOW: 19:00 «Скамейка» — знаменитая пьеса, когда-то блистательно сыгранная Олегом Ефремовым и Татьяной Дорониной на сцене МХАТа, а затем покорившая театральные площадки по всему миру. Это история о мужчине и женщине. О случайной встрече, которая постепенно превращается в откровенный разговор — честный, смешной, ранимый и очень человеческий. О том моменте, когда между людьми исчезают роли и, наконец, становится невозможно притворяться. На сцене — Алексей Панин и Ольга Силина. Тонкая актерская игра, живая энергия и удивительно узнаваемая история, в которой каждый услышит что-то своё. “Скамейка” — спектакль, после которого хочется немного помолчать и еще долго думать о главном. Hidden in plain sight in Chinatown, it’s the kind of place chefs recommend, food writers praise, and regulars quietly keep going back to Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, which is about right. It’s intimate, informal, very good value and usually busy enough to make you feel smug if you’ve managed to get a table without waiting The pho is obviously a very good choice. So are the bánh mì. So is most of the menu, to be honest. But for the next Open Fire Dining Club , Pho Cue are stepping out of Chinatown and heading to Torr Vale Mill for something a little different They’ll be joining Tartuffe on 22 and 23 August for a menu that looks at Vietnamese cooking through a few different routes: the French influence that still runs through parts of the cuisine, the traditional use of fire found across Vietnam, and Cue’s more modern approach to Vietn There’s a continuation from the Porta dinner here too. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

But two of Michael Carrick's first-team players have become subject to shock speculation Having supplanted Ruben Amorim in January, Carrick performed miracles at United's helm last term, guiding them to a third-place finish and Champions League football.
